page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v7 is an Easv7-family memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark data places the E96as_v7 in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as PassMark CPU tests. Memory performance is highly competitive, with small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth reaching the top 10%, while large-block read bandwidth falls in the top 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the top 10%, with Redis achieving 139.15 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference speeds are in the top 10% for small models and top 25% for medium models, though performance drops to average during prompt processing for large 70B models.

From a resource density perspective, the E96as_v7 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound enterprise workloads by combining a high-capacity 768.0 GB RAM footprint with dedicated, high-frequency AMD EPYC compute resources. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage operations rely on network-attached Premium Storage and parallel computing is limited to CPU instruction sets. This profile makes the server suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data-dense enterprise applications, and CPU-driven medium-scale machine learning inference.
